quality.navy->cream: soft: petal structure is present at 2x/3x but mid-tones are greyer and softer than a real cream rose (the 8-bit-crushed navy source carries little shading); smallest/occluded roses 1 and 4 are the weakest
quality.navy->champagne: soft: same source limitation as navy->cream; reads as a satin champagne rose, best on roses 2, 3, 5
quality.cream->navy: flat: dark rose with faint swirl, p90 V clamped into the real navy range; reads correctly at display size

notes: navy/cornflower/cream remeasured on f236 from the label-map pools (median Lab; dark/light = median of the darkest/lightest 15% by L; brief_hex keeps the brief's values). Other colours: brief hex with the brief's dark/light shades. Lab = CIE Lab D65 from sRGB, the same conversion as base_lab.npy and the npz files. Recolour anchors sit at the rose's own t quantiles q10/q50/q90 so the median lands on hex; navy targets have the light anchor clamped so p90 V is within the real navy roses' range [53.0, 87.0]. Navy-source recolours use denoised shading, HF gain <= 1.0 and a stronger local-contrast boost (see fidelity.json class_params).
